ready2_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: In the bridge rectifier capacitor filter circuit shown in the figure, the effective value of the transformer's secondary voltage is \(U_2 = 20\text{V}\). What is the output DC voltage \(\bar{u_L}\)?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: In the bridge rectifier capacitor filter circuit shown in the figure, the effective value of the transformer's secondary voltage is \(U_2 = 20\text{V}\). What is the output DC voltage \(\bar{u_L}\)?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure, the AC power supply is coupled through a transformer, and the secondary side of the transformer is labeled u2; after the secondary side is connected a bridge rectifier circuit composed of VD1~VD4; a filter capacitor C is connected in parallel at the rectified output terminal, the load terminal voltage is labeled uL, and the capacitor and load are connected in parallel at the same terminals, belonging to a bridge rectifier capacitor filter circuit. Reasoning: The given effective value of the transformer secondary voltage is U2 = 20 V. The peak value of the sinusoidal AC voltage is U2m = sqrt(2) * U2 = sqrt(2) * 20 V ≈ 28.3 V. After bridge rectification, the filter capacitor will approximately charge to the peak value of the secondary-side voltage and maintain this voltage between conduction intervals; when ignoring diode voltage drops and ripple, the output DC average voltage is approximately equal to the peak value. Therefore the output DC voltage \bar{u_L} ≈ 28 V.

method.method_draft: First identify from the image that this is a full-wave bridge rectifier followed by a capacitor filter across the load. From the text take the secondary RMS voltage U2 = 20 V. Convert the RMS secondary voltage to its sinusoidal peak: U2m = sqrt(2) * 20 V ≈ 28.3 V. Since the filter capacitor holds approximately this peak between conduction intervals, take the output average/DC voltage as approximately 28 V.
